list.title: Tasks
list.description: Tasks of the current workspace, arranged by group.
list.empty_hint: Create the first one — it will land in its group's section.
list.no_workspace_hint: A task lives inside a workspace. Create the first one — and tasks will appear here.

scope.brief: Search the brief: context, constraints, criteria
scope.plan: Search the agent's work: plan, progress, result and stages

cancel_confirm.title: Cancel the task?
cancel_confirm.text: “{title}” will be marked Canceled: no more work goes into it. To bring it back, change the status on its page.

delete_confirm.title: Delete the task?
delete_confirm.text: “{title}” goes to deleted tasks. To bring it back, turn on the Deleted filter and pick Restore in the task's menu.
delete_confirm.text_children: “{title}” goes to deleted tasks together with its subtasks. To bring them back, turn on the Deleted filter and pick Restore in the task's menu.

conflict.title: The field you are editing has changed
conflict.text: While you were editing, this field was changed in the database — most likely by the agent. The page now shows that version. Your text is below: copy whatever you need, it will be gone once you close this window.

detail.title: Task

hint.description: The gist of the task in two or three sentences: what exactly we build and what result we expect. The agent sees this field in the task list and decides by it whether to open the task in full.
hint.context: Where to start, which code to take as the model, and which decisions are already made and why. As links to files and examples, not retold.
hint.constraints:
Limits on the agent's work: what not to do, what to ask about first and what is mandatory.

For example: log through the module's main logger, ask before adding a dependency, do not create new migrations.
hint.plan: How the agent will do the task: the approach, the details, and which files it has read and will change. Written before the code changes, so the intent can later be compared with what came out.
hint.progress:
How the work is going: the agent briefly notes what is done and what comes next. A new entry is appended at the end; decisions and findings go to the journal.

For example:
— the migration is written, rollback checked → CRUD next;
— API tests fail on the old field → investigating.
hint.result: What was done on the task. The agent writes the result when handing the task over for review: what changed, what checked it, and what is left unchecked.

detail.deleted_note: The task was deleted together with its branch. While it is in the bin, it can't be edited and its status can't be changed.

purge.title: Delete forever
purge.text: The task will be removed from the database for good. It can't be restored.
purge.with_children: The task will be removed from the database together with all its subtasks. They can't be restored.

stage.empty: No stages. Add the first one with the button below — the plan is broken into steps, each with its own evidence.
stage.title: Stage title
stage.evidence_hint: A pointer, not a story: a command and its result, a file path, a diff summary. The stage can't be closed without it.
stage.remove_text: The stage will be removed together with its journal entries. It can't be restored.

note.empty: No entries. This is where decisions made along the way, remarks, findings and things to remember go.
note.title: The point in one line

form.title: Edit group

delete.reversible_without_tasks: Deletion can be undone: the group goes to the deleted list, where it can be restored. The tasks will not come back to it.

ungroup.description: The task moves to "No group" and is otherwise unchanged. | The tasks move to "No group" and are otherwise unchanged.

move.title: Move to another group
move.description: The task and its subtasks move to the chosen group, at the end of its list. | The tasks and their subtasks move to the chosen group, at the end of its list.
move.no_targets: There are no other groups in this workspace — nowhere to move them.
